hard_failure.id: V4-F1 (Source branch override is silently dropped -> Pattern B handover never happens)
hard_failure.summary: The create-wizard's 'Source' field is fully functional in the UI (typed, displayed, submitted) but the resulting dispatched task branches from main's tip, NOT from the typed source branch. The reviewer agent's worktree therefore never contained the V3 dev agent's docs-fix commits, breaking the entire Pattern-B handover premise: 'the branch is the baton'.
hard_failure.assertion_1_sqlite_FAILED: issue.source_branch = NULL and agent_task_queue.source_branch = NULL for the new issue/task, despite the wizard visibly showing 'Source ainb/01KY4F2P90AHH53FJ5HQ3Q70GT' immediately before Enter was pressed. Expected: stored = 'ainb/01KY4F2P90AHH53FJ5HQ3Q70GT'.
hard_failure.assertion_2_git_FAILED: git worktree for the new task (ainb/01KY4G2FWSSF19D45KHKAGZW1J) was created at commit 5cc46072 -- IDENTICAL to main's tip -- not at 29a8245c (V3's branch tip). `git merge-base --is-ancestor ainb/01KY4F2P90AHH53FJ5HQ3Q70GT ainb/01KY4G2FWSSF19D45KHKAGZW1J` returns non-zero (NOT an ancestor). V3's commits are NOT reachable from V4's branch.
hard_failure.downstream_symptom: Because the reviewer's worktree had no docs-fix diff to review, the reviewer agent (with nothing to critique) improvised and committed its own doc regeneration (3a6bc451 'docs(cli): regenerate CLI reference from current binary') directly on top of main inside what it believed was the review branch -- a plausible-looking but semantically wrong outcome that would have silently passed a shallow 'did it commit something' check. This is exactly the kind of failure the harness's fail-closed doctrine (git ancestry, not exit codes) is designed to catch.
hard_failure.confidence: CONFIRMED (not hypothesis) for the observable failure (sqlite + git evidence, reproducible, both assertions independently checked). The EXACT line where the override value is lost is a hypothesis pending deeper trace -- code review traced the full client->wire->daemon chain and found no obvious break, meaning the bug is either a subtle runtime issue (ordering/race between the two RPC legs, or a serialization edge case) or in a segment not yet read line-by-line.
code_pointers_for_fix_agent: crates/ainb-plugin-hangar/src/screen/issue_list.rs:~1594 (wizard_try_create builds IssueListIntent::CreateAndRun{ source_branch: opt(&wizard.source_branch), ... } -- confirmed correct: opt() only special-cases blank, not 'main')
crates/ainb-plugin-hangar/src/plugin.rs:~2530-2597 (apply_create_action stashes source_branch/target_branch into self.wizard_dispatch_in_flight; only fired on the issue_create reply)

crates/ainb-plugin-hangar/src/plugin.rs:~2680-2747 (fire_issue_dispatch: sends TWO RPCs -- hangar/issue_update THEN hangar/issue_run, sequentially over the same unix_socket_send; issue_run's IssueRunParams carries dispatch.source_branch as the override)

crates/ainb-hangar-daemon/src/rpc/mod.rs:1415 handle_issue_update -> issue_field_update_from_params (line 1573): CONFIRMED BUG #1 -- this fn builds IssueFieldUpdate{title,state,assignee,priority,due_date} and NEVER reads params.source_branch / params.target_branch at all, even though IssueUpdateParams has those fields on the wire. The update leg is a silent no-op for source/target branch -- issue.source_branch can never be persisted via issue_update as currently written.

crates/ainb-hangar-daemon/src/rpc/mod.rs:2845 handle_issue_run: DOES read params.source_branch into source_override and pass it into run_card(...) -- this leg should NOT depend on the (buggy) update leg per its own doc comment ('the run is correct even if the persist is still in flight').

crates/ainb-hangar-daemon/src/rpc/mod.rs:3082 run_card: computes source_branch = source_branch_override.or(card_source) and writes it via CardParityRepo::set_task_source_branch_in_tx(&mut tx, &task_id, source_branch.as_deref()) -- traced correct on paper.

NEXT STEP FOR FIX AGENT: since the client->wire->run_card chain reads correct in review but the DB proves the override arrived as None, instrument/trace params.source_branch as actually deserialized inside handle_issue_run for a live repro (add a tracing::info! at daemon entry), OR check for a request-id collision / stream_id race between the issue_update and issue_run sends (both fired back-to-back on the same stream_id without awaiting a reply in between -- verify the daemon's per-connection request dispatch doesn't drop/overwrite params when two requests share worker state).
